chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one who has his hand and leg cut off. He said: He should wash them.

key_terms.الْأَقْطَع: The one who has been cut (amputated)

ai.seo_question: How should one perform ablution if a hand or leg has been amputated?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'washing the remaining part' (ghasl baqi al-darb) for amputees, ensuring ritual validity without requiring the washing of the entire original limb. It reflects the Shia juristic approach of adapting ritual obligations to physical reality, distinguishing between the loss of the limb's function and the requirement for water contact with the existing flesh. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for later fiqh discussions on the extent of washing in wudu for those with partial or total amputation.
